items.title: Houses Above the Ferns
items.idea: A settled human community lives both among the roots and above them. Homes, shared paths and a central gathering place make this a village with an ordinary social life.
items.question: Does this feel like a Genesis village, and which parts of the architecture are worth developing?
items.brief:
A grand, inhabited HUMAN Genesis village in a temperate old-growth forest. View from a gentle wooded slope across a small clearing into five enormous but natural living trees. About EIGHT substantial homes, some on the ground between roots and four modest homes 5–12 metres above the ground, supported on visible broad branch forks and substantial timber brackets. These are human-scale wooden houses with fitted plank walls, steep weatherproof shingle roofs, real windows and modest porches, neither bird nests nor fairy palaces. People have houses, storage, cooking places, privacy and neighbours. Lower homes use stone foundations and timber walls, cared for but individually repaired.
A single clear stair climbs from the ground to a railed landing beside the nearest elevated front door. One short, almost level plank footbridge links TWO visible adjacent house porches at the same height, with both ends supported and obvious; all remaining houses have their own grounded stairs. No disconnected walkways, impossible building tangles, huge suspension system or elves' crystalline city.
The clearing contains a communal table, a roofed bread stall and a patch of beaten earth where small human children play; about ten SMALL human inhabitants distributed naturally, with two adults stopping to exchange news by a doorway. One coherent local community, varied family faces and ages, ordinary linen and wool clothing, no leaf costumes or fantasy-species sampler. Trees are trees, not sentient humanoids.
Composition: wide environmental painting, houses at readable scale within vast trees, human activity as small accents. Fresh silver morning sunlight catches warm honey-coloured wood and cream plaster amid deep blue-green canopy and pale ferns. Light opens a path through the picture. Beautiful, practical and settled rather than uniformly idyllic; patched roof, a shutter being repaired, uneven lanes. No irrigation, giant wildlife or magical glow.

items.title: Voices in the Commons
items.idea: A disagreement over winter stores brings neighbours into the village's common room. Genesis has negotiation and competing needs as well as a relationship with nature.
items.question: Does this kind of social tension belong in Genesis, and does the room feel distinctly theirs?
items.brief:
Inside a forest village's shared meeting hall, six local HUMAN adults are in the middle of a serious disagreement. This is Genesis society, not an assembly of druids or woodland monsters. An oval room with a stout, irregular living trunk rising through an open collar in its fitted timber floor and continuing through a properly framed roof opening; sensible separate beams support the roof, the tree is not a magical ornament. Broad open shutters show leafy branches and the side of another village house at similar height. A bench, a few shelves, woven mats, clay cups and a closed storage chest suggest a place used daily.
Story: a young woman stands at the left end of a scarred rectangular table and places an EMPTY woven grain basket on it, visibly asking for something. Across the table an older broad-faced woman in a plain dark green wool dress holds a heavy iron storehouse key in her open palm but has not handed it over. One middle-aged man leans forward to speak; three other neighbours listen with different degrees of concern and doubt. Restrained disagreement with clear eyelines and distinct hand gestures, not aggression, not cheerful universal consensus. No scroll-map, glowing objects, worship, council crowns or thrones.
Local humans with sun-browned complexions and dark hair, varied ages and body types; same recognisable village community, not identical faces. Clothing is practical flax linen, charcoal wool and occasional muted plant dyes, readable sewn garments with simple fastenings, not layers of random leather, antlers or leaves.
Composition: broad side-on social tableau, faces and empty basket connected by one diagonal of late afternoon light from the window. Warm amber table and skin, cool leafy reflected light, dark plum-grey recesses. Precise expressive paint, consistent resolution across faces and timber. No close-up beauty portraits; the relationship between six people and their shared space is the subject.

items.title: A Room in the Boughs
items.idea: An ordinary morning inside a home in the canopy. A lived-in room tests Genesis through domestic life rather than wilderness alone.
items.question: Does this make life in the trees feel comfortable and believable without becoming too idyllic?
items.brief:
Quiet intimate interior of a modest human home built safely among broad tree branches. Two adult HUMAN sisters in their thirties share a morning before leaving for the day. At left one sits sideways on a low wooden chair and braids her own thick dark hair; two natural hands gather the braid close to her shoulder, simple coherent posture. Her slightly older sister at the back carries two used pottery bowls toward a shelf, paused to speak to her. Neither looks toward the viewer. Familiar ease and a small tired smile, not staged fashion poses or a cute animated family. Individual olive-brown faces, one has a strong long nose, the other a wide face and short hair, modest everyday beauty, ordinary bodies.
Room: fitted timber walls, a narrow sleeping alcove with folded indigo blankets, a clay stove on a square masonry hearth away from wooden walls, a small table with cut fruit and a repaired jug, one coat on a peg. A broad real branch is visible OUTSIDE the open window supporting the house; it does not inexplicably penetrate furniture. Through the window we see another inhabited tree house across leafy space, its lamps now out, and a clear hint of a properly railed porch. Elevated village life is real and recognizable, not solitary survival or a hollow log den.
Subtle imperfection: a neatly stitched patch on a blanket and an old ceiling stain under a repaired roof, but this is a functioning cared-for home. Simple shirts and skirts/trousers, no druid costume, weapons or decorative leaf armour. No creature companion or helpful tree person.
Composition: the open window occupies the upper right and spills a large shape of cool morning light across the women and honey-brown floor; a warm residual ember glow at far left balances it. Muted indigo, russet wood and luminous pale leaf green. Close, finely observed painted domestic scene with soft lost edges and precise small touches, never high-resolution photographic faces.

items.title: The Arena Grown Quiet
items.idea: An imperial arena has become a patchwork of small fields. The present uses the shape of the Empire without restoring its original purpose.
items.question: Is this a worthwhile piece of the lived landscape, and does the old/new scale feel right?
items.brief:
A sweeping high-fantasy countryside landscape showing an ancient imperial arena repurposed into ordinary cultivated land. View from one surviving upper tier down and across a broad oval depression about 180 metres wide. Weathered pale stone seating survives in THREE large incomplete arcs, with realistic human-scale stair risers where visible; most lower seating has collapsed into grassy terraces. The arena floor and broad accessible terraces are now a patchwork of golden grain, pale stubble and a few green kitchen plots. NOT flooded, no canals, no huge pictorial trees, no map symbols.
Four or five tiny human farm workers are cutting and bundling grain in the centre, less than 2% of image height; their one ordinary cart sits on the broad old entrance ramp. A small cluster of maintained rural homes occupies one outer edge above the bowl, built partly from reused stone. Fields have plausible gentle grades and dry retaining walls. One clear continuous access ramp reaches the floor through the remains of an entrance tunnel; no stairs or roads terminate nowhere.
No colossal statue, triumphal arch copied from another image, spectacular ghost, great creature or explanation for the imperial collapse. No banners, tournament, armed force or celebratory crowd. The place feels quiet and inhabited, neither wholly abandoned nor restored to its old power.
Composition: immense curved architectural rhythm against flat far hills and open late summer sky. One bold cloud shadow cuts across the warm oval, changing wheat from ochre to muted olive; pale carved stone, dusty lilac shadow, copper gold and restrained sky blue. Small human work carries emotional scale. A finished traditional landscape painting with broad observed masses, fine selective brushwork and lost edges, almost abstract at the periphery but physically convincing. Avoid excessive archaeological diagram detail, 3D-render sharpness or aerial map conventions.
